title: bug: FileWatcher.ignorePath arms an unconditional 500 ms delete per call, so a daemon write landing 380-500 ms after an earlier write to the same file loses its self-write token to the first call's timer and reloads the whole store under the state mutex as an external edit
description:
Filed by hunt task-afe61cc0 (2026-11-03 #11, lane 3: sweep and reload paths).

PROBLEM
- FileWatcher.ignorePath (packages/moe-daemon/src/state/FileWatcher.ts:50-56) adds the path to a Set and, on every call, arms `setTimeout(() => this.ignorePaths.delete(normalized), 500)`. scheduleChange (:101-105) consumes the token on the first matching event.
- When the daemon writes one file twice, 380-500 ms apart, write 1's watcher event (about 150-200 ms later) consumes the token, write 2 re-adds it, and write 1's still-armed timer fires at t=500 ms and deletes write 2's fresh token. Write 2's event then reaches onChange.
- index.ts:821-830 treats every onChange as an external edit: healMassDeletion's existsSync scan, a full state.load() under the global state mutex (StateManager.ts:1021; today that re-reads 936 task files (29 MB), about 2,200 attempt records and the rest), then a STATE_SNAPSHOT broadcast to every IDE client.
- persistence.ts:15-18 states the contract this breaks: "Registering the ignore before the write is what stops the watcher echoing the daemon's own writes back as external changes." sweeps.ts:174-189 already notes that self-writes leak through and made sweep arming idempotent against it; this is one root cause.

EVIDENCE (HEAD 31492ac5, git-archive snapshot outside the shared checkout; files in /mnt/d/moe-scratch/hunt-afe61cc0/me/)
1. Deterministic repro zzHuntMe_selfWriteTimer.test.ts: fake timers, driving the private scheduleChange that chokidar's handlers call. Sequence: ignorePath t=0, event t=200 (suppressed), ignorePath t=400, event t=550.
   `AssertionError: expected [ { type: 'change', …(1) } ] to deeply equal []` and `Tests 1 failed | 2 passed (3)`. The two controls pass: a single self-write is suppressed, and an external change after the window is delivered. Output: selfWriteTimer.HEAD-31492ac5.out.
2. Real chokidar repro zzHuntMe_selfWrite.test.ts: two ignorePath + atomicWriteJsonAsync writes to one existing tasks/ file. Gaps of 280, 320, 360, 520 and 600 ms are suppressed; 400, 440 and 480 ms each deliver one 'change' to onChange (`Tests 3 failed | 6 passed (9)`). Output: selfWrite-chokidar.HEAD-31492ac5.out.
3. It happens in production. Today's activity log (activity.log.2.gz, .1.gz, activity.log) has 10 same-task write pairs 380-500 ms apart, mostly the wrapper's back-to-back record_commit calls:
   - 2026-11-03T08:48:03.643Z TASK_COMMIT_RECORDED → TASK_COMMIT_RECORDED +398 ms (task-df34243e);
   - 19:49:49.708Z, +415 ms (task-4877ef36);
   - 18:46:07.230Z STEP_COMPLETED → STEP_STARTED +404 ms (task-b22f82b2).
   There are 8 more pairs at 300-380 ms, which the live Windows daemon's slower watcher may also leak. Worker-file writes (heartbeats, chat cursors) are not in the activity log and add to the count.
4. Dry-run fix (not committed): one timer per path (Map<string, Timeout>, clearTimeout on re-arm and on consume) is +7/-4 in FileWatcher.ts. Both repros then pass, and FileWatcher.test.ts plus FileWatcher.paths.test.ts stay green (4 files, 38 tests).

FIX DIRECTION
- Hold one entry and one timer per path: ignorePaths becomes Map<string, NodeJS.Timeout>.
- ignorePath clears any prior timer for that path before arming a new 500 ms one.
- scheduleChange clears the timer when it consumes the token.
- stop() clears the pending timers.
- Keep the 500 ms window and consume-on-first-match, so a later genuine external edit still reloads.

FILES
- packages/moe-daemon/src/state/FileWatcher.ts
- new packages/moe-daemon/src/state/FileWatcher.selfWrite.test.ts

implementationPlan.description:
GREEN: one suppression entry and one timer per path. Edit packages/moe-daemon/src/state/FileWatcher.ts with the Edit tool only. The architect's dry-run diff (+16/-4) is /mnt/d/moe-scratch/plan-bed60fca/FileWatcher.prototype.diff.

(a) Field (:22):
`/** Self-write tokens: one entry and one expiry timer per path. */ private ignorePaths = new Map<string, NodeJS.Timeout>();`

(b) ignorePath (:50-56). After normalizing:
- `const prior = this.ignorePaths.get(normalized); if (prior) clearTimeout(prior);`
- Keep the 500 ms expiry, but guard it so only the current token can delete itself:
  `const t = setTimeout(() => { if (this.ignorePaths.get(normalized) === t) this.ignorePaths.delete(normalized); }, 500);`
- Keep `if (t.unref) t.unref();`, then `this.ignorePaths.set(normalized, t);`.
- Add a comment: re-arm, never stack. An earlier call's timer must not delete the token a later write to the same file just registered, or that write's event reloads the whole store as an external edit (task-bed60fca).

(c) scheduleChange (:101-105):
`const token = this.ignorePaths.get(normalized); if (token) { clearTimeout(token); this.ignorePaths.delete(normalized); return; // Skip self-writes }`

(d) stop(): right after `this.stopped = true;` add
`for (const t of this.ignorePaths.values()) clearTimeout(t); this.ignorePaths.clear();`

Error handling: the change adds no throw path. clearTimeout on an already-fired timer is a no-op, and the timer callback only deletes its own entry. processChange's existing try/catch around onChange (it logs 'FileWatcher onChange error') and the 'FileWatcher error' handler stay as they are.

Keep unchanged:
- the 500 ms window, debounceMs, awaitWriteFinish, the watched-directory filter and path normalization;
- consume-on-first-match, so a genuine external edit after a consumed token still reloads.

Touch no other file. sweeps.ts:174-189 stays as it is: other leaks (an event later than 500 ms) remain possible, and arming stays idempotent.

executionContract.intendedBehavior: FileWatcher's self-write suppression holds exactly one token and one 500 ms expiry timer per normalized path. Re-registering a path (ignorePath) clears its previous timer before arming a new one. Consuming a token on a matching event clears its timer. stop() clears every pending token timer. A daemon write to a file it wrote 380-500 ms earlier is therefore still suppressed after the earlier call's expiry, instead of reaching onChange and triggering a full state.load() plus STATE_SNAPSHOT. A change event for a path with no live token still reaches onChange as before.
acceptanceCriteria: Under fake timers, ignorePath at t=0, an event at t=200, ignorePath at t=400 and an event at t=550 produce zero onChange calls.
A single self-write's event is suppressed.
A change event arriving after the 500 ms window, with no new ignorePath, reaches onChange exactly once.
After ignorePath and stop(), no timer is pending.
invariants: The suppression window stays 500 ms, and a token is consumed by the first matching event.
Path normalization (normalizeEventPath/watchRoot), the watched-directory filter, debounceMs and awaitWriteFinish are unchanged.
Error handling is unchanged: processChange's try/catch around onChange and the watcher 'error' handler.
compatibility: ignorePath's signature and every caller (writeEntity in state/persistence.ts, seedCanonicalChannel, taskStore, workerStore, chatStore, StateManager, purgeResolvedProposals in sweeps.ts) are unchanged.
No MCP or /ws contract changes; only how often a daemon write is mistaken for an external edit.
reuse: No new helper: the existing Set becomes a Map of timers inside FileWatcher.

packages/moe-daemon/src/index.ts:821-830: every onChange runs healMassDeletion, then state.load() under the state mutex, then broadcasts STATE_SNAPSHOT.
Nothing outside FileWatcher.ts reads ignorePaths (grep), and only FileWatcher.test.ts and FileWatcher.paths.test.ts exercise the watcher.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered: (a) A per-path counter instead of a timer map. Rejected: it still needs an expiry, and a timer that outlives its token is the bug. (b) Time-based suppression with no consume (ignore every event for P until a deadline). Rejected: it would also hide a genuine external edit that follows a consumed self-write, which (s3) pins. (c) Widening the 500 ms window. Rejected: it treats the symptom, and a stale timer still deletes a newer token.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights: The bug is the stacked timer, not the window. Write 1's event consumes the token at about 200 ms, write 2 re-adds it, and write 1's timer fires at 500 ms and deletes write 2's token. Write 2's event at about 550-650 ms then reaches onChange. The hunt's real-chokidar repro saw the leak at gaps of 400-480 ms on Linux; the live Windows daemon's slower events widen the window downward. Today's activity log has 10 same-task write pairs in that window, mostly back-to-back record_commit calls. A prototype at 9834628e is +16/-4 runtime and 66 test lines; the base is RED 2/4 ((s1), (s4)), and with the fix 3 files / 30 tests pass.
risks: Without the `=== t` guard in the timer callback, a missed clearTimeout path could still let an old timer delete a newer token. Keep both the clear and the guard.
(s3) must advance past 500 ms before delivering; delivering early would consume the token and hide a regression in the expiry path.
The negative control greps 'Tests  2 failed | 2 passed (4)'. Adding cases changes the count: keep four cases, or update step 4's expected counts.

completionSummary: FileWatcher.ignorePaths is now a Map<string, Timeout>: one token and one 500 ms timer per normalized path. ignorePath clears any prior timer before re-arming, and the expiry callback deletes only its own token (`=== t` guard). scheduleChange clears the timer when it consumes the token, and stop() clears every pending timer. Timers stay unref'd; the window, consume-on-first-match, debounce and error handling are unchanged. New FileWatcher.selfWrite.test.ts has 4 fake-timer cases: (s1) the t=0/200/400/550 sequence is suppressed, (s2) a single self-write is suppressed, (s3) an event after the window reaches onChange once, (s4) stop() leaves no timer pending. Negative control (base source + new test only): "Tests  2 failed | 2 passed (4)" and RED-AT-BASE, with (s1) and (s4) failing. With the fix, tsc is clean and the 3 FileWatcher files pass 30 tests in a snapshot outside the repo.
